patch_description:
Replace the fixed exponentially weighted moving average with a causal adaptive constant-velocity Kalman trend filter. The filter estimates both level and slope, so its prediction step compensates for much of the delay normally introduced by smoothing. Measurement uncertainty is estimated robustly from the recent innovation history using MAD, allowing the gain to decrease during noisy intervals and increase when the signal makes a sustained move. Innovation clipping limits the effect of isolated spikes, reducing noise-induced directional reversals without clipping legitimate broader trend changes.

The returned samples remain aligned with the end of each sliding window, preserving the existing output length and downstream delay assumptions. Computational cost is O(N) with constant-size state updates after initialization.
